title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 12 days after he resigned
dek: Nvidia supplies the chips at the centre of the U.S.-China technology fight. Its founder is back as chief executive, and the White House says the President took part.
what: Update, 25 November 2026. Cointelegraph and WatcherGuru posted that, per the Wall Street Journal, U.S. officials told Congress there is no evidence Chinese intelligence directed the woman tied to Megaspeed to target Huang. I could not open the Journal report or find another outlet repeating it, so this rests on those posts. Earlier paragraphs below say U.S. intelligence agencies were reported to believe she passed information to Beijing. Those were reports, and the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion. EricLDaugh posted that Elon Musk visited Nvidia headquarters with Huang the day after the reinstatement. I found no outside report of the visit.

Update, 23 November 2026. Nvidia says its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately. In its release, filed with the SEC, board chair Harvey Jones says the board believes Huang is "the right person to lead NVIDIA." The release says the board held discussions with Huang, received input from senior U.S. government officials, and is confident his return "poses no national security risk." It also says an independent committee continues to look into a reported foreign intelligence targeting of Huang, that a National Security and Export Control Committee has been set up, and that Nvidia is recruiting a Chief Compliance Officer. It thanks Colette Kress for her service as interim CEO; she keeps her CFO role.

On 17 November, the Associated Press reported Jones as saying the board "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." The AP also reported that Huang agreed to appear before House committees on 1 December and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter on 2 December. I did not find a statement from Nvidia that explains what changed in six days beyond the release above.

President Trump, in a statement the White House account posted, called the board's decision "correct and proper" and said the country needs Huang's leadership. A post of the full statement also has him saying the government has no reason to believe Huang's return poses a national security risk. I could not see the rest of that statement. Per a post, the White House also says Trump joined a board meeting and "intervened" to advocate for the return. I found no Nvidia statement confirming that, and the release speaks only of input from government officials. In remarks the account atrupar posted, Trump says he has been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly," and, on CNBC, that his administration gave the board "assurance" on the national security question. Those are Trump's statements and I could not check them against another source.

Elon Musk posted "It is done" and, per Cointelegraph, "The mistake has been corrected." Musk had said earlier that he was signing the petition for Huang's return. In nothing I found has the Justice Department said whether it now considers the woman a spy; Trump's statement refers to the Attorney General, but I could not read what it says about that. Posts also say Nvidia shares rose sharply on the news. I did not check a price or a market value, and I give none here.

On 24 November, the Financial Times reported that Trump may have gained between about $1.3 million and $15 million on Nvidia shares on Monday, when Huang was reinstated. The paper based this on Trump's financial disclosures, which cover holdings through 30 September and show up to 370,000 shares in ranges. The gain is on paper and does not reflect a sale, per a summary of the report by JFeed. I could not open the Financial Times article. Trump told CNBC, "I spoke to them, let me put it that way... And I convinced them." Senator Ruben Gallego called for an investigation into whether Trump "put our national security on the line" for personal gain, per the same summary. I found no White House reply. The disclosure ranges are wide and Trump's holdings today may differ from those on 30 September.
The paragraphs below are the earlier record, as of 16 November, and are kept for context.

Nvidia's filing with the SEC (a Form 8-K, event date 11 November 2026) says the board accepted Jen-Hsun (Jensen) Huang's resignation as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim CEO while keeping her CFO role, and the board has begun a search for a permanent CEO, internal and external. Harvey Jones was named board chair. The filing gives no reason for the resignation and does not mention the investigation. Polymarket posted the news on 12 November.

On Sunday, 8 November 2026, CNBC and Fox Business reported that Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation of chief executive Jensen Huang. The reports say Huang emailed staff: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her" and "I am deeply sorry." WatcherGuru posted extracts of the email.

CNBC says the woman is tied to Megaspeed, a cloud company and Nvidia customer that has been investigated over whether it helped restricted Chinese firms get Nvidia chips. CNBC and others, citing The New York Times and the Financial Times, say U.S. intelligence agencies believe she passes information to Beijing. I could not see those original reports, and I found no statement from her. She is not named here. The 8-K does not say whether the investigation has ended.

Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised." It said a committee of independent directors, helped by outside counsel, will examine all available information. On 8 November a spokesperson said Huang remained committed to staying on as CEO; the 11 November filing replaced that. Gavin Baker, an investor, posted the board's statement.

Three House Republican committee chairs have asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on 18 November, according to CNBC and RedState. Cointelegraph posted that President Trump called Huang "an honorable guy" and wants to hear his side. I could not confirm that remark outside X.

After the resignation, KTLA and Fox Business report that President Trump wrote on social media: "there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" Cook announced in April that he would step down as Apple's chief executive and is now its executive chairman. I found no Nvidia comment on the idea.

Reuters reported on 12 November, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee. Newsweek, summarising Reuters, says Reuters did not name her or describe her role, and that Nvidia declined to comment. She is not named here. CNN also reported on a second relationship; I could not open the original reports, and I could not confirm her reporting line. On the evening of 12 November, Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters the Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion on whether the woman tied to Megaspeed was a Chinese spy, and that the FBI is looking into the reports, per Reuters via U.S. News. The same report says Beijing has denied she is a spy. On 13 November UTC, Cointelegraph posted that Kress will meet staff next Wednesday, the morning after Nvidia posts quarterly results. I found no outside source for that.

A volunteer-run site called Stand with Jensen, which is not endorsed by Nvidia or Huang, has a petition asking the board to reinstate Huang or give evidence-based reasons, run a fair investigation with clear timelines, and share its concerns. The Hans India reports more than 43,000 signatures, including current Nvidia employees and shareholders, as counted by the petition. Elon Musk posted that he is signing it. The Hans India reports no response from the board. The count changes and I did not check it. Polymarket posted on 14 November that the petition had passed 100,000 signatures. I did not check that count. Business Upturn reports the petition showed 151,282 signatures on 15 November, and that its site says affiliations are self-reported and unverified. Business Insider, per the same report, found apparent joke or false entries. Business Upturn quotes an Nvidia statement: "A growing online appeal does not, by itself, change who is running Nvidia."

Musk also posted that Huang "drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," and that without him some of them are at risk. That is Musk's opinion of Nvidia's supplier arrangements. I found no Nvidia statement on it.

On Sunday, 15 November 2026, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures, as Reuters reports, that Nvidia's board "need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup." Reuters also says he called for the board and outside counsel to answer, within 10 days, questions about the company's culture of compliance with export restrictions. Reuters, citing the Financial Times, says the board has approached Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas. I could not open the Financial Times report and Nvidia has not commented in anything I found. WatcherGuru and others posted Bessent's remarks within minutes. The Washington Post is also reported, in a post by the account kimmonismus, to say Huang is helping find his successor; I could not confirm that outside X.

On the evening of 15 November UTC, the Kobeissi Letter posted that the Financial Times reports Huang is considering a return as CEO while the board investigation continues, and that an ally is organising a group of tech executives to lobby for it. I could not open the Financial Times report or find another outlet repeating it, so this rests on that post.

Other posts, including a video from the account Nostre_damus, claim Huang leaked chip secrets. No source I found says so, and the board says it has no reason to believe it. That claim is not supported here.
why: It joins a personal admission to the question of whether a chip maker's top executive was compromised, while Congress is already pressing Nvidia on exports to China.
next: Huang is due before House committees on 1 December and Nvidia's general counsel on 2 December, per the AP. The independent committee has not said when it will finish. The Justice Department has not said whether it considers the woman a spy. Nvidia has not said what the White House role was beyond "input."

corrections.text: Added the 25 November reports that U.S. officials told Congress they found no evidence China directed the woman, marked as resting on posts.
The story said Huang was staying on as CEO. Nvidia's 8-K of 11 November says he resigned as CEO and director effective immediately; Colette Kress is interim CEO. Title and text updated.

Added Trump's post naming Tim Cook and Attorney General Blanche's statement that the Justice Department has not concluded whether the woman was a spy. The earlier text said the Cook remark rested on posts only.
The earlier text said the second employee reported to Huang. Reuters, as summarised by Newsweek, gave no role for her, so that detail is removed and the report is now attributed to Reuters.
Added the reinstatement petition and Musk's post signing it.
Added the petition count Polymarket posted and Musk's remark about supplier deals.
Added Bessent's remarks of 15 November and the reported approach to Rene Haas.
Added the reported Financial Times item on a possible Huang return, marked as resting on a post.
Added the petition count of 15 November, the caveats on it, and Nvidia's reply to the petition, from Business Upturn.
Huang was reinstated on 23 November. Title, summary, status text and the next steps updated; the earlier paragraphs are kept as the record up to 16 November.
Added the Financial Times report of 24 November on Trump's possible gain from Nvidia shares, with its limits.
